correctness.rationale: The source defines all 48 edges of each graph and exhausts all 2^16 assignments per graph by four-row formulas. The exact cut histograms yield delta coefficients 16,-96,240,-384,672,-1344,2016,-1920,1104,-352,48 for q^12 through q^32; multiplying 16q^12(q²−1)^8(3q^4+2q²+1) gives precisely these. Independently reimplemented the complete 65,536-mask census with a separate adjacency edge construction, checking edge count 48, full coefficient factorization, and max-cut counts R=90 S=42 at c=32. Algebra Z=e^(48K)P(e^(-2K)) gives strict positive difference for nonzero real K; equality at K=0. Exact binomial transform gives common even-subgraph coefficients through degree7 and 19602−19506=96 at degree8. This exhaustive finite proof is valid for exactly these two finite graphs, not a claim about all graphs.

value.rationale: A canonical smallest nonisomorphic strongly regular cospectral pair provides a substantive test of whether adjacency spectrum controls Ising thermodynamics. The exact factorization establishes a strict ordering for both signs of coupling, a sharp first discrepancy in high-temperature degree, and different antiferromagnetic ground-state degeneracies. This natural finite comparison can be valuable even without a general graph theorem; complete 2^16 enumeration is a valid finite proof.

final_claim: For cospectral rook K4□K4 and Shrikhande (16,6,2,2), P_R(q)-P_S(q)=16q^12(q²−1)^8(3q⁴+2q²+1), hence Z_R(K)>Z_S(K) for every real K≠0; the first even-subgraph difference is 96 at degree 8 and maxcut counts are 90 versus 42.
limitations: Uniform coupling and zero external field on precisely two 16-vertex graphs; both ferro- and antiferromagnetic real K.
